question: Can training computation be reduced online by detecting when each neuron's input-output behavior has stabilized and temporarily omitting that neuron from parameter updates?

key_findings.claim: Neuronal equilibrium is operationalized as stability of a neuron's validation-set output geometry across epochs, not as small weights or gradients.
key_findings.evidence: For each neuron, normalized activations over a fixed validation subset are concatenated and compared by cosine similarity between consecutive epochs; a momentum-filtered change in that similarity defines the equilibrium signal.

anchors.section: 3.1 Neuronal equilibrium and 3.2 Neuron dynamics evaluation

key_findings.claim: The update mask is reversible and adapts after learning-dynamics changes.
key_findings.evidence: A neuron is frozen when the absolute velocity of its similarity change is below epsilon, but it is made trainable again if a later epoch violates the threshold, for example after a learning-rate change.

anchors.section: 3.3 Selection of trainable neurons at non-equilibrium

key_findings.claim: NEq reduces reported backward-pass FLOPs across CNN, transformer, classification, and segmentation settings with small final-metric changes.
key_findings.evidence: Across five runs, ResNet-32/CIFAR-10 falls from 138.94M to 84.81M backward FLOPs per iteration (-38.96%) while accuracy changes from 92.85% to 92.96%; ResNet-18/ImageNet falls 23.08% with -0.28 points, Swin-B/ImageNet falls 64.39% with -0.36 points, and DeepLabv3/COCO falls 28.77% with -0.49 mIoU.

key_findings.claim: The learned equilibrium mask outperforms random freezing at a matched average FLOP budget in all four reported setups.
key_findings.evidence: The Stochastic* control receives the achieved compute budget after the fact, yet its final metric is lower than NEq in each Table 2 row; this isolates some value in which neurons are updated rather than only how many.

key_findings.claim: The paper establishes algorithmic FLOP savings, not end-to-end hardware acceleration or energy savings.
key_findings.evidence: Results report average back-propagation FLOPs and final task metrics. They do not report wall-clock time, memory traffic, total training energy, the cost of epoch-wise validation activation collection, or speedups from kernels that exploit changing neuron masks.

method.core_idea: Temporarily stop updating whole neurons whose validation-response relationship has reached a stable regime, while keeping their forward contribution active.
method.mechanism: After every epoch, run a fixed validation subset, form one normalized response vector per neuron, update consecutive-epoch cosine similarity and its momentum-filtered velocity, and mask backward updates where the absolute velocity is below epsilon; recompute masks so neurons can unfreeze.
assumptions: Stability on a small validation subset reflects stability of the useful learned function
A cosine-based output statistic distinguishes converged behavior from harmless rescaling
Skipping a whole neuron's gradient can be implemented without offsetting overhead
Epoch-level masking reacts quickly enough to optimizer and learning-rate changes
Freezing individual neurons does not disrupt coupled group dynamics

techniques.role: Measures whether a neuron's input-output relation has stopped changing across epochs.
Smooths the epoch-to-epoch equilibrium statistic before thresholding.
Skips updates for full neurons while allowing later reactivation and retaining all forward activations.
Separates neuron selection quality from the raw fraction of updates omitted.

evaluations.metric: average backward FLOPs per iteration and top-1 accuracy
evaluations.baseline: dense baseline at 138.94M FLOPs and 92.85%, plus compute-matched stochastic freezing at 86.34M and 92.23%

limitations: Author-stated: equilibrium is assessed neuron by neuron even though groups may have collective dynamics not visible in isolated statistics.
Author-stated: the underlying training schedules were borrowed without tuning for compute savings, so the achievable frontier remains uncertain.
Only backward FLOPs are measured; wall-clock, memory, monitoring, communication, and energy costs are absent.
The method consumes a validation subset during training and may indirectly tune to it.
The epsilon threshold is task-dependent: large values sharply reduce compute but also accuracy in the ablation.
Validation-size robustness is shown mainly on homogeneous convolutional CIFAR features and may not transfer to heterogeneous data or token models.
failure_modes: A neuron's cosine direction is stable while its scale changes in a way that matters downstream.
A small or unrepresentative monitoring set marks a specialized neuron as converged prematurely.
Coupled neurons look individually unstable even when their subspace is stable, or individually stable while their joint role is not.
Dynamic fine-grained masks cause irregular kernels and memory traffic that erase theoretical FLOP savings.
A sudden optimizer, augmentation, or distribution shift occurs between epoch-level checks.
reusable_insights: Distinguish removing a unit from inference from merely stopping its optimizer updates.
Use reversible compute allocation when the identity of useful parameters changes during training.
Compare adaptive update policies with random policies at the same realized compute budget.
Validate efficiency claims with total wall-clock and monitoring overhead in addition to operation counts.
Behavior-space convergence can reveal redundancy that weight magnitude or gradient magnitude misses.
open_questions: Can equilibrium be measured for learned subspaces or attention heads rather than individual neurons?
What kernels and batching strategies convert changing structured masks into real accelerator speedups?
Can threshold selection be made budget-aware and calibrated without consuming a held-out set?
Does activation equilibrium predict safe freezing in language-model pretraining and distribution-shifted training?
How much of the reported accuracy-compute frontier remains after charging the monitoring forward passes?

competitive_landscape.title: FreezeOut: Accelerate Training by Progressively Freezing Layers
competitive_landscape.difference: FreezeOut freezes layers permanently according to a predetermined schedule and reports wall-clock results; NEq uses data-dependent neuron-level masks that can reverse when dynamics change, but reports FLOPs rather than realized time.

competitive_landscape.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Lottery tickets identify an unstructured subnetwork through train-prune-rewind cycles and then train it in isolation; NEq does not remove forward connections or rewind and decides online when full neurons need updates.

competitive_landscape.title: SNIP: Single-shot Network Pruning Based on Connection Sensitivity
competitive_landscape.difference: SNIP uses one initial loss-sensitivity pass to permanently select individual connections before training; NEq monitors activations throughout training and reversibly freezes structured neuron updates.

competitive_landscape.title: Coarsening the Granularity: Towards Structurally Sparse Lottery Tickets
competitive_landscape.difference: Structured lottery tickets use iterative magnitude pruning plus refill/regroup post-processing to create a permanently sparse inference graph; NEq preserves the dense inference graph and targets backward-update savings during a single run.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: NEq is an online, structured, reversible way to stop unnecessary neuron updates without a pretrained model, pruning-retraining loop, or fixed schedule.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Activation-dynamics masks adapt across optimizers and learning-rate phases and beat matched random freezing across four training setups.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive combination is behavior-based neuron granularity plus unfreezing during the same training run. The evidence supports a better backward-FLOP allocation rule, but not yet practical training acceleration because monitoring overhead and hardware execution are unmeasured.

reviewer_notes: Read all 13 extracted pages, with a second pass on the equilibrium statistic, mask reversibility, epsilon and validation-size ablations, every Table 2 row, and stated limitations. Primary records for FreezeOut, lottery tickets, SNIP, and structured lottery tickets were checked.
